BiblicalUsage: Tattenai was the Persian governor west of the Euphrates who challenged the rebuilding of the temple. He asked the Jews who commanded them to build this house, and wrote to Darius about it; and Darius answered that Tattenai was to let the work of the house of God alone, and the governor did as the king commanded.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the governor who came to stop the work ended up carrying the king's order to let it alone.
